notes: **A button's label** longer than 20 characters is cut short by the adapter, with an ellipsis. The click still sends the whole choice.

settings.description: The token Meta sends back when it checks your server's address: any text of your own, entered as the webhook's Verify token.

addressGoes: the Meta app's dashboard → WhatsApp → Configuration → Callback URL, with WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN as the Verify token, subscribed to messages

why.maxTextLength: WhatsApp refuses a text of more than 4,096 characters. The adapter splits a longer one itself (WHATSAPP_MESSAGE_LIMIT), but only at a line break: text with none is cut at the 4,096th character, through the middle of a word. 4,000 is within the limit, so the cut is made here, where the text breaks.
why.settings: The verify token is the caller's own choice: Meta is given it with the address, and sends it back in the GET it checks the address with (hub.verify_token), which the adapter compares with this setting.
why.addressGoes: The adapter makes no call that registers the webhook: a person enters the address and the verify token on Meta's page, and Meta checks it with a GET the adapter answers, so the server has to be running.
why.capabilities: WhatsApp shows three reply buttons on a message. The adapter sends the first three and drops the rest, and says nothing (extractReplyButtons: buttons.slice(0, MAX_REPLY_BUTTONS)).
